key_insight: DSQ improves GPCR ligand bioactivity prediction by embedding a physics-based MWC allostery model into a dual-state neural query architecture that separates active and inactive receptor behavior.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a more interpretable way to predict agonism and affinity for drug discovery, especially when high-resolution active-state structures are unavailable.
method: Learnable orthogonal queries extract disentangled active-state and inactive-state latent representations.
A neural MWC gating module converts ligand-state affinities and receptor conformational energy into activation probability.
A contrastive ranking loss enforces physically consistent differential affinity ordering.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that DSQ outperforms baselines, with especially strong gains on the agonist subset, and includes homology-stratified, temperature-sensitivity, perturbation, clustering, and efficiency analyses.
watch_item: Performance is limited on low-homology receptors, so generalization may weaken when receptor sequence similarity to training data is small.
paper_title: GPCR Ligand Bioactivity Prediction with Physics-Informed Dual-State Query Learning
